general_fitness.directive: General fitness must be full body, safe, sustainable, and full body biased; use full body A/B structure, Zone 2, mobility, and simple double progression.

volume.beginner: 2-3 sets per exercise, 6-10 hard sets per major pattern weekly
volume.intermediate: 3-4 sets per exercise, 8-14 hard sets per major pattern weekly
volume.advanced: 3-5 sets per exercise, tempo or density add-ons only when recovery allows

general_fitness.progression: Double progression: add reps first, then load; keep technique clean.

bodybuilding.directive: Bodybuilding must be hipertrofi focused: structured mechanical tension plus metabolic stress, not random split volume.

volume.beginner: 8-12 sets per muscle weekly with machine bias
volume.intermediate: 12-18 sets per muscle weekly with compound plus isolation balance
volume.advanced: 16-24 sets per muscle weekly only when recovery allows

intensity.advanced: Advanced intensity techniques only on isolation work

bodybuilding.progression: Double progression plus cautious weekly set additions for intermediate and advanced users.
bodybuilding.deload: Every 4-6 weeks reduce volume 30-50% and cap RPE at 6-7.
bodybuilding.fatigue_rule: Control chest/shoulder/triceps overlap and leg-day systemic fatigue.

powerlifting.directive: Powerlifting must treat squat, bench, and deadlift as ana kaldırış anchors with planned exposure and fatigue control.

volume.beginner: 3 day technique-first exposure, 2-4 main lift sets
volume.intermediate: 4 day split with heavy and volume exposures

powerlifting.progression: Add reps before load; upper lifts +2.5-5%, lower lifts up to +5% when bar speed and RPE allow.
powerlifting.deload: Every 4-6 weeks reduce volume 30-50% and intensity 10-15%.
powerlifting.fatigue_rule: Do not peak squat and deadlift in the same week; monitor deadlift CNS fatigue.

crossfit.directive: CrossFit must be structured energy system training: strength, skill, gymnastics, conditioning, and controlled chaos.

volume.beginner: 50-70% WOD volume, lighter load, longer rest
volume.intermediate: Full WOD standard with moderate load
volume.advanced: Higher density, barbell cycling, and advanced gymnastics

intensity.advanced: Metcon RPE 8-10 with recovery days mandatory

crossfit.progression: Increase density or complexity only after movement quality is stable.
crossfit.deload: Every 4-6 weeks reduce WOD volume and high-intensity density.
crossfit.fatigue_rule: Never place two high-intensity days back to back.

calisthenics.directive: Calisthenics must use progression tree logic for neural and mechanical skill acquisition.

volume.beginner: Assisted progressions, shorter holds, submaximal sets
volume.intermediate: Strict bodyweight movements with full ROM and moderate volume
volume.advanced: Weighted movements, isometric holds, high density circuits

intensity.intermediate: Strength days RPE 7-8, skill days RPE 5-6
intensity.advanced: Circuit days RPE 8-9, skill work low fatigue

calisthenics.progression: Do not skip skill dependencies; map movement to the next safe progression.
calisthenics.deload: Reduce pull volume and circuit density every 4-6 weeks.
calisthenics.fatigue_rule: Control pull-up volume and avoid failure because form breakdown is costly.

functional.directive: Functional training must be movement pattern based: motor control, unilateral stability, mobility, and transfer to daily life.

volume.intermediate: 3-4 sets plus unilateral and circuit density
volume.advanced: Higher load, tempo, density, and complex circuits

functional.progression: Increase reps, tempo control, stability demand, then load.
functional.deload: Every 4th week reduce circuit rounds and loading.
functional.fatigue_rule: For low conditioning, reduce circuit volume and increase rest.
